summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Reported to House):

blocks.text: 504 Modernization and Small Manufacturer Enhancement Act of 2026

This bill generally expands the Small Business Administration (SBA) 504 Loan Program to include additional objectives and flexibilities (e.g., new qualifying economic development objectives). The program provides a small business with SBA financing—through a certified development company (CDC) intermediary—for expansion or modernization.

Specifically, the bill expands the public policy goals that allow a CDC to qualify for assistance to include additional objectives. These include (1) workforce development through work-based or work-integrated training, and (2) aiding the revitalization of an area for which a disaster has been declared or determined.

The bill also authorizes a CDC to take specified actions to facilitate the closing of 504 loans, such as correcting borrower or lender information on loan documents or reallocating up to 10% of the cost of a project.

Further, the bill allows small businesses to lease a larger portion of renovated buildings that are financed with 504 loans to other tenants in certain circumstances. In the case of a project to renovate or reconstruct an existing building, a small business may lease a maximum of 66% of the building to commercial or residential tenants if certain conditions are met. For example, the small business must have occupied the building for 12 consecutive months prior to the project.
Additionally, the bill exempts CDCs from the requirement to demonstrate they are unable to obtain credit elsewhere to receive 504 loans.

The 504 Modernization and Small Manufacturer Enhancement Act of 2026 would broaden the Small Business Administration's 504 Loan Program, which helps small businesses pay for expansion or modernization. Under the program, a small business gets SBA-backed financing through a certified development company, or CDC, that acts as an intermediary.

The bill adds new public policy goals that can qualify a CDC for assistance. These include workforce development through work-based or work-integrated training, and helping revitalize an area where a disaster has been declared or determined.
The bill also lets CDCs take certain steps to help close 504 loans. These include correcting borrower or lender information on loan documents and reallocating up to 10% of a project's cost.

In addition, the bill lets small businesses lease a larger share of renovated buildings financed with 504 loans to other tenants in some cases. When a project renovates or rebuilds an existing building, the business may lease up to 66% of the building to commercial or residential tenants if certain conditions are met. One example condition is that the business must have occupied the building for 12 consecutive months before the project.
Finally, the bill exempts CDCs from having to show that they cannot get credit elsewhere before receiving 504 loans.
